title: Prove sharp binary-stream faithfulness thresholds
body:
Formal address tests describe full binary streams only when the group-algebra action is faithful. This contribution proves the sharp boundary for diagonal actions on w point columns: GL_d(F2) requires w>=d and AGL_d(F2) requires w>=d+1 for d>=2, with both dimension-one exceptions explicit. A regular orbit recovers every coefficient of every dirty-register endpoint. Below the boundary, the nonzero group norm annihilates all payloads.

The failure is realized by a literal two-register GL2 word with 18 paid coordinate CNOTs and 10 free scalar XORs. Its formal map is I+n_G E_01, yet at w=1 it is identity on every input. At w=2 six input columns expose the coupling. This is an interface theorem and legal-word control, not a claim that a particular monomial target becomes cheaper.

The source-bound corollary transfers PR1974's credited 28,224 two-register GL3 minima to this declared full binary bit-plane action at every w>=3. It preserves the predecessor's alphabet, pricing and endpoint; the third-register result retains its existing length-seven limit. PR1974 is pinned at a4992da8e4e81a74cf1fd2b2d3af948662476d6e and PR1333 at 7f25b6d0e1d7e995d4d2840f231d98b1a1a9fec2. Their exact retained README bytes are authenticated. The prior census, affine rank theorem and homogeneous-image norm alias are credited, not rerun or counted as new results.

Validation passed on native CPython 3.12.7 and 3.14.5: 19 complete orbit cases, formal word replay, all 40 dirty input columns, 18 omitted-paid-call controls, and four export/source/typed-receipt groups. The registered 3.12.7 command is:

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/binary-stream-faithfulness
```

Independent AI review imported no candidate executable: it checked all 5,376 point-tuple stabilizers, direct algebra-action ranks in 14 small cases, the literal word and every dirty input column. No material issue was found. Exact review and source receipts are retained with delivery; no human or formal-kernel certification is claimed.

Scope is explicit: affine translation is shared by all point columns, scalar mixing remains optimistically free, and payloads are arbitrary full streams. Arithmetic modulo q^w, rational frames, restricted subspaces, physical conversion/compiler costs and selected supplier admission are outside this result. No frontier or multiplication exponent changes.

Canonical main 0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2 and priority revision 4 were refreshed before packaging. At 2026-10-15 15:42:39 UTC both source heads were unchanged; the latest 50 open PRs and target comments were screened. Complete Discussion coverage remains the explicitly dated cached snapshot from 12:29:05 UTC because GraphQL quota prevented a fresh full scan. The canonical claim is https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1974#issuecomment-6195671518.

Credit Josie Elliston, Hanson Sun, Gareth Davidson and the standard regular-orbit/orbit-stabilizer arguments. Prepared for ywz65 with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0.
